item.title: Nordic Consumer Culture
item.content:encoded:
The Nordic region exhibits a distinctive consumer culture marked by paradoxes: societies balance egalitarian values with status-consciousness, individualism with collective welfare systems, and modesty with aspiration. The Nordic welfare state uniquely aligns state and individual interests, creating a distinctive marketplace. Despite growing research examining Nordic consumption patterns—from branding and cultural phenomena to alternative food markets and immigrant experiences—significant gaps remain in understanding how these contradictions manifest across consumption practices and market formations.

This special issue seeks to advance comprehensive scholarship on Nordic consumer culture by publishing novel and critically grounded research that explores the interplay between state, market, and consumer practices. The editors welcome contributions analyzing market dynamics, investigating paradoxes inherent in Nordic consumption, and examining how macro-level contexts including welfare policies, cultural myths, and political ideologies shape consumer behavior, with particular interest in innovative methodologies and interdisciplinary approaches.

Appel publié par Qualitative Market Research An International Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • State-market-consumer relations and welfare consumption
  • Neoliberalization and privatization of welfare services
  • Nordic imaginaries, myths, and branding
  • Sustainability, nature consumption, and friluftsliv
  • Immigration, minorities, and consumer integration
  • Indigenous consumption and colonial legacies
  • Gender, family, and domestic consumption practices
  • Egalitarianism, conformity, and status distinction
  • Consumer resistance and alternative markets
  • Digitalization and platform consumption
  • Dark consumption, Nordic Noir, and dystopian aesthetics
  • Trust and distrust in state institutions
  • Nordic brands and cultural exports
  • New Nordic movements and manifestos
  • Contradictions in Nordic consumer culture

  • December 20, 2026: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Research with Impact: Qualitative approaches to social and behaviour change
item.content:encoded:
Elina Närvänen, Tampere University

Ariadne Kapetanaki, University of York

Anoop Bhogal-Nair, De Montfort University

This special issue seeks qualitative research that goes beyond traditional market analysis to address systemic social equity and behaviour change. The collection aims to demonstrate how interpretive methods can tackle complex social problems that quantitative data alone cannot solve, emphasizing participatory frameworks and deep engagement with marginalized populations. The issue argues that qualitative research serves not merely as a descriptive tool but as a transformative force for inclusive change.

Contributors are invited to submit work employing rigorous qualitative and interpretive approaches to understand lived experience, uncover behavioral motivations, and engage with under-represented groups. The issue responds to a critical need for research methodologies that empower neglected populations and address challenges such as climate anxiety, public health inequities, and trauma-informed perspectives on social change.

Appel publié par Qualitative Market Research An International Journal. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Innovative qualitative approaches to design and/or evaluate social marketing initiatives
  • Qualitative approaches for inclusive research
  • Participatory approaches (action research, co-design)
  • Difficult, sensitive, or stigmatised topics and sensemaking through qualitative methods
  • Ethics of participatory inclusive methods for behaviour and social change
  • Longitudinal qualitative frameworks for social impact of ethical interventions

Timeline

  • January 10, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • December 15, 2026: Closing date for manuscripts submission
